title: For n>=3 and c>=1, the (c,c)-dimensional, one-framed Lambda_n quiver moduli at theta=(2c,1-2c) consists entirely of the Hilbert-scheme component cut out by f_1=...=f_(n-1)=0
author: Claudio Bartocci; Ugo Bruzzo; Valeriano Lanza; Claudio L. S. Rava
source_title: On the Irreducibility of Some Quiver Varieties
difficulty_reason: The substantive obligation is to rule out every singular matrix pencil in a framed stable representation, rather than merely invoke irreducibility of a Hilbert scheme. The author constructs alternating generated subspaces from a minimum-degree polynomial kernel vector and treats the zero-framing and nonzero-framing cases by different stability contradictions, including an SO(2,C) normalization and an induction using the quiver relations. This supplies the new global exhaustion of a quiver-moduli component and is substantially beyond standard qualifying-exam linear algebra or GIT definitions.
source_version: Official SIGMA 16 (2020) article 069, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2020.069; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-09-30, exact bytes pinned by SHA256

proof_review.method: Published author proof/core and local context fidelity screening
proof_review.note: The full new regular-pencil argument in Proposition 3.6 was read: a least-degree polynomial kernel vector generates alternating subspaces, and the two framing cases contradict the two numerical stability conditions. The SO(2,C) normalization and the induction controlling the generated odd subspaces are explicitly supplied. Lemma 3.7 transfers subobjects through the quotient algebra, and Theorem 3.8 uses the previously published equivalence between the regular-pencil locus and H(n,c), explicitly located in [1, Proposition 4.9 and Theorem 4.5]; that established equivalence is background rather than an omitted new step. The selected n>=3 branch excludes the already known n=2 case and does not count the intermediate regularity lemma separately.

statement_scope: Exactly the n>=3, c>=1 branch of Theorem 3.8 over C, for Lambda_n=CQ_n/J_n with the arrows and relations of Section 3, dimension vector (c,c), framing dimension 1 and theta_c=(2c,1-2c). H(n,c), defined by all f_q=0, equals the entire moduli. The previous Hilbert-scheme identification is supplied as context; no separate claim is counted.
